maya: FYI ran long-context 32k regen tests across hosted/dedicated/private. Noticed sustained KV growth on Dedicated after ~600s.
chris: can you share flamegraphs / pmap? :thinking:
maya: link: https://grafana.redwood/ps/abc123 — looks like many PTEs pinned; heap grows until OOM on dedicated 8xA100 test
olga: what kernel / MTU / hugepage settings on the dedicated cluster?
maya: Dedicated: Ubuntu 22.04, kernel 6.1.0-43, MTU 1500, hugepages enabled (2M), jemalloc 5.3.0. Hosted run used 6.1.0-28 container host, MTU 9000 (ENIs), transparent hugepages off.
diego: interesting. jumbo frames on hosted could reduce pagefault churn. Also how's batch sizing during generation?
maya: We force batch max_tokens=64, adaptive batching on. Profiling shows kernel selection fallback to scalar matmul at long seqs (seq>8k) on dedicated which spikes per-step latency and causes cache churn.
chris: can you paste the perf snippet? maybe the memory ops are coming from prefix/KV allocation pattern.
maya: ```perf top sample:
  32.4% kv_store_reclaim
  18.1% kv_page_fault_handler
  11.2% copy_user_generic
  6.4% tensor_copy_kernel
```
olga: kv_store_reclaim high implies evict loop thrashing. Are we hitting different reclaim thresholds between deployments? config drift?
maya: yes — dedicated had aggressive reclaim_age=30s vs hosted 120s. Private (on-prem) had reclaim disabled (0) due to earlier OOM mitigation.
diego: disabling reclaim on private could cause long-term growth but avoid fragmentation churn — what did private show?
maya: Private (on-prem) with older kernel 5.15 and NVLink showed stable usable memory but a plateau higher than hosted. No repeated page-in/page-out loops.
chris: hypothesis: dedicated config + kernel 6.1 kernel changed hugetlb behavior -> reclamation path takes heavier locks -> increases latency -> batching backpressure -> KV allocations pile up.
maya: I also saw differences in jemalloc arena behavior: dedicated had higher rss because arenas not being reclaimed across threads; overlayfs containerization reduced MADV_DONTNEED efficacy.
olga: next steps: 1) run repro with identical reclaim_age/jemalloc on a dedicated node, 2) flip MTU to 9000 on dedicated test, 3) add a kernel-level perf (ftrace) around reclaim path.
jennifer: +1. Also add a canary config that pins kernel-selected matmul to optimized kernel path to see if that prevents thrash.
maya: I've queued a test run (job/kv-longrun-1723). Will post results. thanks :thumbsup:
